panels.title: Cost this month so far (from recorded watts)

panels.description: Recorded watts of both plugs added up since the billing period began on 23 Oct 2026. The plugs were installed 25 Oct, so the first two days are not counted. This is the project's share, not the whole home.

panels.description: Same energy times the rate chosen at the top.

panels.title: Projected to the next reading (18 Nov): cost

panels.title: Project share of latest bill: energy
panels.description: Both plugs' 7-day average power carried over 30 days, divided by the latest whole-home bill's kWh (213.93). The bills before the plugs include some of this load already, so read it as a share, not as extra cost.

panels.title: Project share of latest bill: cost
panels.description: The same, in dollars at the chosen rate, over the latest bill's total ($55.19). The marginal rate leaves out the fixed customer charge, so it reads lower than the all-in rate.

panels.title: Project energy per 30 days (7-day average)
panels.description: Both plugs, from the last 7 days (or all the history there is if shorter).

panels.title: Idle floor: cost per month
panels.description: The 5th-percentile combined power of the last 7 days, counting only moments when both plugs read (about what both machines draw doing nothing), carried over 30 days at the chosen rate. This part is paid whether or not the harness runs.

panels.title: Above idle (harness and gaming): cost per month
panels.description: 7-day average power minus the idle floor, over 30 days at the chosen rate. This is the cost of actually using the machines.

options.content:
**Rates (from the owner's AES Ohio bills, 2026-04-28 to 2026-10-22; derived by Claude, not billed per-kWh figures [UNVERIFIED]):**
- The default rate is the **marginal** $0.2124/kWh: supply $23.22 + other delivery charges $22.22 over 213.93 kWh on the latest bill, leaving out the fixed $9.75 customer charge (assumes other delivery charges scale with kWh). The **all-in average** ($55.19 / 213.93 kWh) is $0.2580/kWh. Pick either in the `rate` list at the top. A straight-line fit over six bills gives about $9.52 + $0.2024/kWh. The billing-period boxes use the dates in the hidden `bill_start`/`bill_end` values; update them and this list when a new bill arrives.

**What the PC plug feeds:** a power strip with the PC, two screens, an unmanaged switch, a lamp (almost never on) and a laptop charger (sometimes). All of it is in the "PC" numbers.

**Colours:** green / orange / red appear only where there is a fault threshold (status, memory, disk, server CPU, ping, uptime after a restart, CPU speed while busy). Power, energy and cost are blue because more is not a fault. The PC's CPU is blue because a busy PC means the harness is working.

**Estimate vs bill:** the row under the billing boxes compares the plugs' recorded energy with the latest whole-home bill, and the chart plots actual cost so far against the projected total for this bill period.

**Plugs:** both plugs report watts, volts, amps and energy (server `192.168.1.66`, PC `192.168.1.6`). The cost charts accumulate only from when each plug was installed, and a projection from a short history is rough: the PC's draw changes a lot with harness load and gaming.

**Not here yet:** the PC's GPU load, replay-archive size and Loki logs. Big-number view for the screen: dashboard "Hiveplex at a glance (kiosk)".
